# Temple Scroll Column 58 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 58 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**58:1** They shall sit before him and he shall take counsel with them in every matter of Torah and judgment that comes to the king.

**58:2** And he shall heed their counsel and act according to the Torah and according to the judgment and according to the statute which they declare to him.

**58:3** And if the king hears that any nation or people is plotting evil against his people Israel,

**58:4** he shall send to the council of the princes and to the priests and to the Levites, and to all the heads of the people,

**58:5** and they shall come to him, and he shall take counsel with them, and they shall go out together with all the men of war.

**58:6** And he shall set commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds and commanders of fifties and commanders of tens in all their cities.

**58:7** And from the sons who are twenty years of age and upward he shall select the men of war, and he shall send them out to battle;

**58:8** and the aged and the fearful-hearted they shall not send among them.

**58:9** And they shall not go to war without taking counsel, and they shall be guided in everything by the council.

**58:10** And all the spoil and plunder they shall give to the king and to the princes and to the priests and to the Levites and to all the army, each his portion.

**58:11** And when the king hears of a conspiracy from far or from near, from any place within the borders of the land that I am giving to them,

**58:12** he shall gather the army and go out to meet them, and the fear of the LORD shall be upon the nations,

**58:13** and the king shall judge with righteous judgment, and he shall not show partiality in judgment.

**58:14** And his wife — she shall be from the house of his father, from his family; one wife from his father's house; and he shall not take another wife besides her, only her alone.

**58:15** And she shall be with him all the days of her life; and if she dies, he shall take another from the house of his father, from his family.

**58:16** And he shall not pervert the judgment of any, and he shall not take a bribe.

**58:17** And he shall write for himself all his judgments upon a scroll, and it shall be before him and before the council all the days.

**58:18** And if the king acts treacherously against the Torah, then the council shall rebuke him and say to him: Return from your evil way.

**58:19** And if he does not return, then they shall bring him before the great assembly, and they shall judge him.

**58:20** And the king shall not put anyone to death by his own authority, but only upon the word of the council.

**58:21** And the king shall be subject to the Torah and to the council, and the council shall be subject to the Torah of God.

---

*EMET notes: Column 58 continues the Temple Scroll's unique Law of the King. The mobilization procedures (58:3-10) reflect an idealized tribal military structure. The spoil distribution includes priests and Levites — characteristic of sectarian revision. The accountability mechanism (58:18-19) — the council may rebuke the king and bring him before the assembly — is unprecedented in biblical law. The restatement of monogamy (58:14-15) reinforces the key sectarian concern.*
